This app calculates and shows its data without a server. The catalog, the curves and the hydraulic engine are inside the APK.
Start and stop only walk the schematic. They do not start a real ESP.
Capabilities declared by the schematic. A false value is not implemented.
Status declared by the pump view
This view has no quantitative model. Pressure, head and power are calculated in Physics Lab.
Downhole motor, at the lower end of the assembly. It turns cable power into shaft rotation and drives the pump. The model does not represent power, current or speed.
Turns electrical energy into mechanical energy.
Power, current, voltage, pole count and efficiency: data still missing. These are not calculated values.
The shaft carries motor rotation, through the protector and the intake, to the impellers. Without poles or a nameplate rating, speed and torque are not calculated.
Drive between the supply and the cable. This control stores a study frequency; it does not simulate an operating point.
Study range: 30 to 90 Hz. This is not a real drive limit.
Frequency must be a number from 30 to 90 Hz.
This value does not calculate a new flow rate, head or power. The pump curve at this frequency and the system curve are both missing.
Synchronous speed is 120 × f / poles. The model has no pole count, so rpm is not calculated.
REDA catalog curves are published at 60 Hz and 3500 rpm. Changing this frequency does not shift them.
A frequency change can change motor speed and, with it, pump flow and head. That relation is not calculated here.
The pump animation stays illustrative. It does not change with this frequency.
Static hydraulics. The numbers come from the bundled engine, the same hydraulics-v0.1 model.
From 1 to 120. A teaching ceiling, not a manufacturer limit.
Q is an input of this experiment. It does not yet come from a pump curve.
Result calculated with %1$s. It is not a nameplate value.
Hydraulic power is not the curve shaft power and it is not motor electrical power.
In this model Q is an experiment input.
Static calculation. There is no change over time.
ΔP is the pressure increase from intake to discharge. A positive value means discharge pressure is higher than intake pressure.
Head is energy per unit weight, written as an equivalent height. It is not a physical column standing on the pump. At the same ΔP, a lighter fluid gives a larger head.
Power the model associates with the fluid hydraulic-energy increase. With constant density, ρ g Q H and Q ΔP describe the same result. It is not electrical power and it does not include efficiency.
Ideal learning simplification: total head is shared in equal parts. It does not claim that every real stage produces the same head in every condition.
Enter a valid number in every required field.
Pressure cannot be negative in this educational model.
Unknown pressure unit. Use Pa, kPa, bar or psi.
Density must be greater than zero.
Unknown flow unit. Use m3/s, m3/day or bpd.
Stage count must be an integer greater than or equal to 1. In the lab the selector stops at 120.
Unknown head unit. Use m or ft.
Unknown power unit. Use hp or kW.
Enter a name for each fluid.
Discharge pressure does not exceed intake pressure. The calculation continues, but this is not the case of a pump driving fluid.
Flow rate is zero. Hydraulic power is zero because there is no flow.
The sheet is per stage. Without a stage count the lab total head is not compared with this curve.
The laboratory flow is outside the digitized segment. It is not extrapolated.
The interpolated efficiency cannot estimate shaft power.
The curve is referred to the sheet specific gravity. It is not viscosity-corrected and it is not presented as valid for another fluid.
Approximate digitization. The sheet warning is below.
The pressure difference is the same. Head differs because H = ΔP / (ρ g) and density is not the same. Pressure and head are not synonyms.
The pressure difference is the same and so is the head, because the compared densities produce the same result.
The pressure differences do not match, so head is not compared at constant ΔP.
Three curves of the same model, speed and setup, read on the same flow rate.
Changing the study frequency does not shift these curves.
Empty: the sheet stays per stage. An integer ≥ 1 estimates the total when the basis is per stage.
No curve is included. Turn on a selector to see the chart.
There is no sheet for that combination.
Estimate: per-stage sheet head and shaft power multiplied by N. Efficiency is not multiplied.
Without a stage count the lab head is not marked on a per-stage sheet.
Shaft power read on the curve: %1$s %2$s
This is not the published shaft power. It does not include motor or drive losses.
The nearest digitized sample is shown. Points outside the segment are not invented.
Chart of head, shaft power and efficiency against flow
Slide the chart sideways if it does not fit. The three vertical scales are independent.
ESP Digital Twin is an educational and experimental platform for the progressive study of electrical submersible pump systems.
This mobile version carries the same catalog and the same static engine. It does not call a server to calculate.
Hybrid Physics-AI Model for Sensorless Monitoring and Anomaly Detection in ESP Systems.
Modelo híbrido Física-IA para monitoreo sin sensores y detección de anomalías en sistemas ESP.
Roadmap 1A–1F is included. The numeric engine is still static hydraulics. There is no dynamic simulation and no AI model.
Pressure difference, head and hydraulic power
Downhole motor. Power, current and poles are still missing.
Study frequency. It does not calculate an operating point.
Student of the Master in IT and Telecommunications Management — Universidad Andrés Bello (UNAB), Chile.
Machine learning, physics-informed models, an operational digital twin and anomaly detection are not part of this app.
ESP Digital Twin is a research, learning and simulation platform. It does not control a real ESP. The models may include simplifications that belong to each educational stage.
